summary: Forest Lookouts list describes a native-stone tower built by CCC workers on Mount Scott; no build date, status or site description found.

facts.design: Tower built of native stone (per Forest Lookouts; no date or height given)
facts.status_note: None of the sources says whether the stone tower still stands.
facts.agency: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (Wichita Mountains National Wildlife Refuge)

access.note: Wikipedia says visitors can reach the summit by car or bicycle on a three-mile paved road. No source says whether the tower itself can be entered.

visit.trail_note: Wikipedia says hiking is allowed with no formal trails, and that the paved road is open to walkers and cyclists only from 6 to 9:30 a.m.

evidence.quote: A tower built using native stone, the work performed by members of the Civilian Conservation Corps.

notes_for_editor: The story rests on one undated line from the Forest Lookouts list. Nothing found gives a build date, height, status, staffing, or fate. Lead to check before publishing: Living New Deal describes a stone CCC lookout called Lake Jed Johnson Tower about three miles west of Mount Scott (https://livingnewdeal.org/?p=186973). The page returned 403 to fetch_text and was not read or cited; if it describes the same structure, the Mount Scott record may be misplaced. The NHLR Oklahoma list (5 registered lookouts) has no Mount Scott entry. The Wikipedia paved-road hours may be out of date.
